summary: Implemented and behaviorally verified (live on hamsa) the 3 agent-executable phases: scope-wrapping claude launcher (packages/claude-code.nix), liveness-only reaper module (modules/home/services/claude-session-reaper.nix) with decoy-based tests, and the static build gate (nix flake check, nixos-rebuild build, home-manager build all pass). Phases 4-7 are USER-EXECUTED (sudo rebuild switch, real interactive wezterm session, live process kill) and were not attempted. Phase 8 depends on 6-7's verbatim output and is not started. The release-gating Phase 7 negative test has not run.

blockers.description: Phases 4-7 require sudo (nixos-rebuild switch), a real interactive wezterm terminal session, and live process manipulation (kill a session, observe orphan death, observe a live long-running child survive repeated reaper runs). None of these can be performed by an agent. Phase 8 (docs + rollback path) additionally depends on Phase 5-7's verbatim observed output and cannot proceed until they are run.

decisions_made: --collect omitted from the systemd-run invocation after live empirical testing on hamsa showed no observable difference in scope-unit auto-unload behavior on this systemd version, with or without the flag, on clean and non-zero exit.

Reaper script adds two ambiguity checks beyond the plan's numbered steps (unparsable PID list, PID vanished mid-read) that both skip the unit, to satisfy the binding constraint's 'any ambiguity' clause literally for those named cases.

Decoy construction for the live-session behavioral test required 'bash -c "sleep 600; true" claude-decoy-marker' rather than 'exec -a claude-decoy sleep 600': exec -a fails under this host's multi-call coreutils wrapper, and a bare 'bash -c sleep 600' gets tail-call exec-optimized by bash into a bare sleep process that loses any argv0 marker.

Phases 1-2's plan-specified 'behavioral, not eyeballed' verification (standalone script exercise, hand-made live/abandoned decoy scopes) was performed directly via Bash on this live host, since hamsa has a working systemd --user session -- this is distinct from and does not substitute for Phases 4-7's requirement of the real claude launcher, sudo, and a real interactive terminal.
dead_ends: exec -a <name> <cmd> for decoy argv0 spoofing -- fails under NixOS's multi-call coreutils wrapper ('coreutils: unknown program ...').

A single trailing command in `bash -c '<cmd>'` for a decoy expected to keep bash's own PID/cmdline visible in cgroup.procs -- bash's tail-call exec optimization silently replaces the bash process with the final command, discarding any marker; append a harmless trailing command (e.g. '; true') to force a real fork.
